name: Art of Problem Solving
line: AoPS teaches hard problems one course at a time. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs Art of Problem Solving: AoPS teaches through hard problems, one course at a time. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous.
verdict: Art of Problem Solving teaches through hard problems, one course at a time: the family picks a course, the learner works through its lessons, and full solutions sit in a separate manual [3][5]. In AMP, assessment and teaching are continuous. Every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test and no test day. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level and sets the next problem. In AoPS Online, the family picks a course from the schedule, and the course sets the lessons [3]. Alcumus, its practice site, is described as adaptive. We found no description of how it chooses problems [2].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything a learner needs hangs off the problem in front of them: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a film where there is one, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In AoPS Online the unit is the course, taken in a live class that meets once a week or at the learner's own pace [3][4]. In the books, problems come first and their full solutions are in a separate manual [5].

reasons.title: Feedback on every answer
reasons.body: After every answer AMP shows whether it was right, the correct answer and the worked steps. Answers are checked exactly, and the next problem is chosen with that answer in mind. With AoPS books, the work is checked against a separate solutions manual, which gives full solutions, not just answers [5]. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, at several ages and in several subjects, feedback that explains had the largest average effect [9].

reasons.title: A level for each part of math
reasons.body: AMP keeps a separate level for each part of math, on one map of skills from counting through precalculus. A learner further along in one part than another gets work at both levels, and repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on. AoPS works one course at a time, each on one subject, such as prealgebra, counting and probability, or geometry [3]. A live class meets once a week for a set number of weeks [3][4].

rows.range: Grades 5 to 12: prealgebra through calculus, plus contest, physics and programming courses, one course at a time [1][3].
rows.start: The family picks a course from the schedule [3].
rows.teaching: Problem-first textbooks, with full solutions in a separate manual [5]. Live classes that meet weekly with an instructor, or self-paced courses [3][4].
rows.next: The next lesson in the chosen course [3]. Alcumus is described as adaptive; we found no description of how it chooses [2].
rows.mastery: None found in the pages we read [2][3][5].
rows.review: Courses are organized by subject [3]. No scheduled review of earlier topics found in the pages we read [3][5].
rows.print: Textbooks and solutions manuals, the same for every reader [5].
rows.adult: With the books, the work is checked against the solutions manual [5]. A live class has an instructor at a set weekly time [4].
rows.evidence: No outcome study found on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [1][6][7].

theirs: Art of Problem Solving (AoPS) is a math education company with texts, online classes and more for grades 5 to 12 [1]. It aims past the usual course: its Prealgebra text says it goes much deeper than a traditional middle-school course and prepares students for contests such as MATHCOUNTS and the AMC 8 [5].

Its books are written problem first, and a separate solutions manual works every problem in full [5]. AoPS Online offers courses one at a time, from prealgebra through calculus, plus contest, physics and programming courses. A learner takes a course in a live class that meets once a week, or at their own pace [3][4]. Alcumus is its online practice site, pitched at high-performing students [2]. This page covers the books, the online courses and Alcumus.
credit: Hard problems, taken seriously. Its courses stress depth and rigor and prepare students for math contests [4][5].
Every book problem has a full worked solution, not just an answer [5].
Live teachers lead weekly classes, from prealgebra through calculus [3].

theirs: We found no outcome study of AoPS's books, online courses or Alcumus on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [1][6][7].
ours: Two findings bear on this comparison. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, at several ages and in several subjects, feedback that explains had the largest average effect, 0.49, against 0.32 for the correct answer alone and 0.05 for right or wrong only [9]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, practice that mixed and spaced topics scored 62% a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [8]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and the code is public.

them: Your child loves hard problems and wants a weekly class with a teacher, working toward math contests.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate tests.
You want every answer checked at once and followed by the worked steps.
You want learned skills to keep coming back, mixed with other math.
Your learner is at different levels in different parts of math.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Art of Problem Solving?
questions.answer: AoPS teaches through hard problems, one course at a time. The family picks the course, and full solutions sit in a separate manual [3][5]. AMP has no separate test. Every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills come back in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Art of Problem Solving work?
questions.answer: We found no outcome study of its books, online courses or Alcumus on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [1][6][7].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, wherever they are in an AoPS book or course.
